title: Score HACOR
formula:
The HACOR Score is calculated by the addition of the selected points:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H eart rate, beats/min | ≤120 | 0 |
| ≥121 | 1 | |
| A cidosis (pH) | ≥7.35 | 0 |
| 7.30–7.34 | 2 | |
| 7.25–7.29 | 3 | |
| <7.25 | 4 | |
| C onsciousness ( [GCS](nabda:calc.glasgow-coma-scale-score-gcs\) ) | 15 | 0 |
| 13-14 | 2 | |
| 11-12 | 5 | |
| ≤10 | 10 | |
| O xygenation ( [PaO₂/FiO₂](nabda:calc.horowitz-index-lung-function-p-f-ratio\) ), mm Hg | ≥201 | 0 |
| 176–200 | 2 | |
| 151–175 | 3 | |
| 126–150 | 4 | |
| 101–125 | 5 | |
| ≤100 | 6 | |
| R espiratory rate, breaths/min | ≤30 | 0 |
| 31–35 | 1 | |
| 36–40 | 2 | |
| 41–45 | 3 | |
| ≥46 | 4 | |

how_to_use.why: Aide à prédire la probabilité d’échec de la VNI, ce qui aide les cliniciens dans la prise de décision précoce concernant la poursuite ou l’intensification de l’assistance respiratoire.
how_to_use.when: Best used in critically ill patients with acute hypoxic respiratory failure who require NIV, helping predict the risk of NIV failure.
how_to_use.pearls: While the score’s accuracy may vary depending on the underlying cause of respiratory failure, it has been derived and validated in multiple disease states, including pneumonia, pulmonary edema, COPD, and ARDS.

next_steps.advice:
- This tool should not be used as the sole determinant for intubation; consider it alongside clinical judgment and other indicators.
- For patients with a high score (>5), early intubation may reduce in-hospital mortality.
- If NIV appears successful (score ≤5), maintain close monitoring and consider other supportive measures to optimize respiratory function.
- Reassess the patient frequently, as changes in the score over time may indicate a need for escalation.

more_info:
Interprétation :

| Score HACOR | Risque d'échec de la VNI |
| --- | --- |
| ≤5 | Faible |
| >5 | Élevé |
